title: Define delivery SLAs and accountability tiers for company OKR initiatives
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: create a lightweight, enforceable set of delivery SLAs (timelines, escalation paths, and success signals) and a three-tier accountability model for all company-level OKR initiatives so cross-functional teams have clarity on commitments and escalation behavior.

Context: repeatedly during Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 we saw misaligned expectations between product, engineering, and design on initiative delivery windows (canary vs full rollout), which caused delayed launches and noisy executive escalations. This ticket codifies standards that balance predictability with engineering reality: SLA bands (Target / Alert / Breach), who owns each band, escalation ladders, and automatic corrective actions (e.g., pause rollout, rollback, or scope reduction).

Scope: company-level OKRs and any initiative tagged with "company" priority. Does NOT change team-level sprint SLAs. Primary stakeholders: PM, Eng leads, Design lead, People Ops for RACI, and Sales/Customer Success for downstream comms.

Why now: upcoming cross-org initiative planning for Cycle 45 and Dedicated capacity product line requires a clear, repeatable framework to avoid ad-hoc executive escalations and to improve forecasting for resource commitments.
acceptance_criteria: A written SLA spec exists that defines three bands (Target, Alert, Breach) with concrete time and qualitative thresholds for common initiative types (feature launch, dedicated capacity contract, private deployment rollout).
A one-page accountability tier chart (Tier 1: Exec-owned OKRs; Tier 2: Cross-functional initiatives; Tier 3: Team-scoped projects) with named roles and responsibilities is published to Confluence.
Escalation playbook documented with decision trees and sample Slack/Email templates for Alert and Breach conditions.
Metrics and dashboards wired: a simple OKR initiative tracker that surfaces SLA status (green/yellow/red) per initiative in the Console PM dashboard and a weekly digest for execs.
Pilot: framework applied to 3 upcoming initiatives (one per tier) for the next cycle and retrospective notes collected.
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng Director (Sana Morales), Design Lead (Renee Ortiz), and Revenue Ops (Jordan Blake).
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha K: Drafting initial goals and scope. Spoke with Sana M and Renee O about common failure modes (slow infra rollouts, unclear rollback ownership).

2025-02-16 Sana Morales: Eng feedback — SLA must account for infra-led dependencies (kernel deploys, quantization jobs) and include runway for A/B experiments. Recommend 'Alert' trigger at 40% slippage not 20%.
2025-02-17 Renee Ortiz: Design concerns — release gating should include a UX sign-off node to avoid partial shipping of flows that block users. Added to doc.
2025-02-18 Jordan Blake: Revenue ops — ask that we include customer communication windows for Alert vs Breach. Will create templates.
2025-02-19 Liam C: Incorporated feedback, created Confluence page (link below), and opened GH PR for dashboard wiring. Preparing pilot plan for three initiatives.
decisions: Adopt three SLA bands: Target (planned cadence), Alert (early warning, requires PM+Eng sync), Breach (exec escalation).
Accountability tiers: Tier 1 = Executive sponsor + PM (company OKRs), Tier 2 = Initiative owner (PM) + Eng/Design leads, Tier 3 = Team lead.
Automatic actions: on Alert -> weekly gating meeting; on Breach -> pause rollout and run rollback checklist unless exec waives.
Alert threshold adjusted per feedback: use relative slippage (e.g., >40% behind baseline) and qualitative blockers rather than strict calendar days for infra-heavy initiatives.
